item.title: Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known…
item.description:
Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known that hatred is a defilement of the mind, abandons hatred, the defilement of the mind; having known that dullness and drowsiness are defilements of the mind, abandons dullness and drowsiness, the defilements of the mind; having known that restlessness and remorse are defilements of the mind, abandons restlessness and remorse, the defilements of the mind; having known that doubt is a defilement of the mind, abandons doubt, the defilement of the mind. This, householder, is called a noble disciple of great wisdom, of wide wisdom, one who has entered the domain of clear vision, possessed of wisdom. This is called being complete in wisdom.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.61

item.title: Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed,…
item.description:
Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed, bound, tangled like a ball of thread, like a matted cocoon, like twisted muñja grass and babhaja reeds, unable to escape from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, birth and death.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.199

item.title: Sātāgira: The sage's mind is fully accomplished, His deeds are perfectly done. Let us approach the Venerable Gotama, Fully possessed of wisdom and good conduct.…
item.description:
Sātāgira:
The sage's mind is fully accomplished,
His deeds are perfectly done.
Let us approach the Venerable Gotama,
Fully possessed of wisdom and good conduct.

Hemāvata:
His calves are like an antelope's, lean and steady,
With little food, not greedy, absorbed in jhāna.
Let us go and see the seer Gotama
Who practices jhāna in the remote forest.

Alone, like a lion, like an elephant, not grasping at pleasures,
Let us approach and ask him about release from the snare of death.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.9

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these five benefits for a patient person. What five? People love him and like him; no one hates him; not many people…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these five benefits for a patient person. What five? People love him and like him; no one hates him; not many people avoid him; at the time of death his mind is not confused; after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Bhikkhus, these are the five benefits for a patient person.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.215

item.title: 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen greed not arise, or arisen greed is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'The sign of the…
item.description:
'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen greed not arise, or arisen greed is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'The sign of the foul.' For one who gives wise attention to the sign of the foul, unarisen greed does not arise, and arisen greed is abandoned. This, friends, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen greed and for the abandoning of arisen greed.' 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen hatred not arise, or arisen hatred is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'The liberation of mind by loving-kindness.' For one who gives wise attention to the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, unarisen hatred does not arise, and arisen hatred is abandoned. This, friends, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen hatred and for the abandoning of arisen hatred.' 'For what reason, friends, for what condition does unarisen delusion not arise, or arisen delusion is abandoned?' The answer should be: 'Wise attention.' For one who gives wise attention, unarisen delusion does not arise, and arisen delusion is abandoned. This, friends, is the cause, this is the condition for the non-arising of unarisen delusion and for the abandoning of arisen delusion.'

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.68

item.title: Bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of form. Of feeling…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, an unlearned ordinary person does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of form. Of feeling ... of perception ... of formations ... He does not truly understand the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of consciousness. Bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple truly understands the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of form. Of feeling ... of perception ... of formations ... He truly understands the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape of consciousness.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.74

item.title: Young householder, keeping bad company has six dangers: gamblers, libertines, drunkards, swindlers, deceivers, and violent persons are his friends and companions. Young householder, such are…
item.description:
Young householder, keeping bad company has six dangers: gamblers, libertines, drunkards, swindlers, deceivers, and violent persons are his friends and companions. Young householder, such are the six dangers of keeping bad company.

item.title: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu have increase of wealth? Bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu have increase of wealth? Bhikkhus, here a bhikkhu abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in all respects, he abides pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. He abides pervading with a mind imbued with compassion ... with a mind imbued with altruistic joy ... He abides pervading with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. Bhikkhus, thus a bhikkhu has increase of wealth.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 26 – Cakkavatti­sīhanādasutta

item.title: - Bhikkhus, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness.…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is a support for the establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is the production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Thus is the origination of this whole mass of suffering.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38

item.title: If an elder bhikkhu, Kassapa, does not delight in the training, does not praise undertaking the training, and does not encourage those bhikkhus who do…
item.description:
If an elder bhikkhu, Kassapa, does not delight in the training, does not praise undertaking the training, and does not encourage those bhikkhus who do not delight in the training, and does not genuinely and timely praise those bhikkhus who delight in the training — such an elder bhikkhu, Kassapa, I do not praise. Why is that? Because other bhikkhus might associate with that elder bhikkhu, thinking: 'The Teacher praises him.' And those who associate with him might adopt his views. And those who adopt his views would bring about their own long-term harm and suffering. Therefore, Kassapa, I do not praise such an elder bhikkhu. If a middle bhikkhu, Kassapa ... If a junior bhikkhu, Kassapa, does not delight in the training, does not praise undertaking the training, and does not encourage those bhikkhus who do not delight in the training, and does not genuinely and timely praise those bhikkhus who delight in the training — such a junior bhikkhu, Kassapa, I do not praise. Why is that? Because other bhikkhus might associate with that junior bhikkhu, thinking: 'The Teacher praises him.' And those who associate with him might adopt his views. And those who adopt his views would bring about their own long-term harm and suffering. Therefore, Kassapa, I do not praise such a junior bhikkhu.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.91
